lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
personal.mjs: 6 files, 2,604,574 B, of which chunks/localDate-D0qIlCcC.mjs is 2,468,700 B (94.8 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 663,774 B in 105 modules, 13.4 % of the static path of teamhub.mjs, imported by its root in 124 files: App.vue (NcAppContent, NcAppNavigation, NcAppNavigationCaption, ...), components/ActivityFeedView.vue (NcAvatar, NcButton, NcEmptyContent, ...), and 122 more. It is imported per module as well, through 4 other specifiers.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.
Written against: vue 3.5.43, 24 delivered packages; @fullcalendar/core 6.1.21, 6 delivered packages.
Other delivered libraries: 96, vue-material-design-icons 5.3.1, interactjs 1.10.27, axios 1.20.0, sortablejs 1.14.0, date-fns 4.3.0, marked 14.1.4, and 90 more.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
